name: Maciej Brzeski
intro: Frontend engineer with ~10 years building business web applications in Angular, React and TypeScript. I also make small browser games.
summary: Frontend engineer with ~10 years building business web applications, specialising in TypeScript single-page apps with Angular and, over the last ~2 years, React.

Grew from Junior to Lead over nine years at EPAM Systems, leading engineering teams and delivering products used by over a million people. Works across the stack with Python when a feature needs it, and uses AI coding tools in everyday development.
In my own time I build small browser games, LLM-agent tooling and edge-AI gadgets.

highlights.label: users of one app I delivered

points: Delivered enterprise business applications for international clients, primarily Angular / TypeScript single-page apps, including one serving 1M+ users.
Built with Angular 17–18, using Standalone Components, RxJS and NgRx, on Nx monorepos with Angular Material and SCSS.
Built production features in React and TypeScript, managing client-side state with Redux and Zustand.
Improved front-end performance, cutting time-to-first-paint from several seconds to near-instant.
Drove code quality across large codebases, reducing linter and compiler errors from hundreds to a handful.
Led engineering teams, owning technical direction, solution design, code review and mentoring.
Over the last ~2 years extended into full-stack delivery across Angular / React front-ends and Python back-ends.
Built responsive websites, CMS solutions and interactive front-ends with JavaScript, AngularJS, Node.js, PHP and WordPress.
Manager, DTA (company management, recruitment, partner relations).
Lab assistant, Jagiellonian University crystallography lab and HeidelbergCement.

projects.title: probevane
projects.text: Harness that adds unit and e2e tests to a codebase through a gated LLM agent loop, with stack adapters including React and Angular and a mutation-tested gate: the agent only finishes once its tests catch real bugs.

projects.title: 1st place, QAHub AI Hackathon 2026
projects.text: Built an LLM-agent pipeline generating UI and API test cases and Playwright automation.

projects.title: This site
projects.text: Prerendered to static files with signals, zoneless change detection and Material 3 theming; the games are separate bundles.

projects.title: pdfmotion
projects.text: Component library for PDFs that animate in Acrobat, Chrome and Firefox and stay still everywhere else. Tested in real viewers with Playwright.

projects.title: percept
projects.text: A wearable environment analyser that runs vision models on-device.

games.title: Duck Gallery
games.blurb: Carnival shooting-gallery roguelite. Six slots on the counter, weapons and modules buff their neighbours, and some pairs combine (wet + burning = steam). Hit the ticket quota every round or get thrown out of the fair. 15 rounds to win.
games.controls: Move the sight with the mouse, or drag on touch; your guns fire on their own. P or Esc pauses, M mutes. Spend tokens at the prize stand between rounds.

cad.description: 3D-printable parts I design as CAD scripts, drawn in the browser with my own wireframe viewer.
cad.intro: Parts I design for my 3D printer. They are written as CAD scripts rather than drawn by hand, and each script also writes the assembly you see here. Turn them, explode them, and point at a part to read its note.
cad.credit: Drawn with hologrid, my small three.js viewer: every part is sliced by a 10 mm grid in the orientation it prints in, and hard edges are traced on top.

models.title: 3D scanner, rig 2
models.blurb: A laser-line 3D scanner on a free-standing frame of reused Ender 3 aluminium extrusions: a fixed camera on a leadscrew carriage, two line lasers on a head bar and a 258 mm turntable. Layout draft: some printed parts are still blocks for size.

models.title: Scanner turntable
models.blurb: The turntable for a 15 cm scan volume. AprilTag markers sit in keyed pockets on the face and on a faceted calibration lip; a reused Ender 3 stepper motor drives it directly.

models.title: 3D scanner, first design
models.blurb: An earlier design draft: a desk-clamped post carrying a SCARA arm with a pan/tilt wrist, and a head with a Raspberry Pi camera, a Pi Zero 2 W and two cross lasers.

models.title: Desk post
models.blurb: A fully printed post that clamps to a wooden desk: three 270 mm square tubes on pinned couplers, and a carriage that pins into holes every 50 mm.

models.title: Morphwheel tread
models.blurb: A flexible TPU tread loop with 52 PLA cores, made in one print: the printer pauses and the cores are dropped into their pockets.
